There's a calibration problem European founders run into the first time they interview US sales candidates.

On our latest episode of Human-First, James Isilay describes it well:

American salespeople are trained to *sell themselves* with a level of confidence and polish that European candidates rarely match... it's the cultural baseline in the US, not a differentiator.

For a European hiring manager, that's disorienting. You're used to candidates who undersell. Now you're sitting across from someone who has clearly rehearsed and you can't easily tell whether what you're hearing reflects real performance or a well-built pitch.

The fix is rigour. Press into what they actually delivered. Ask specific questions about their sales process and how they run a deal. Treat performance claims as starting points for diligence, not finish lines.

And reference check thoroughly, with people who saw them sell, not just people they handed you.

The cost of getting this hire wrong in a new market is **much higher** than the cost of slowing down to verify.

Cold calling in 2025 is harder than ever. Our latest 2025 benchmark report shows that cold call success rates dropped nearly 50% from 2024. 

From our analysis of 200,000 cold calls we learnt:

- Sellers aren’t taking the time to understand the prospect's challenge or situation
- Economic buyers are more reluctant to purchase software
- There is more competition than ever before
- Sellers are spending time on the wrong prospects
- Buyers are more educated than they’ve ever been

In short, it’s a tough market - but sellers are making it harder for themselves.

The data doesn’t lie.

A positive for Cognism is that our global success rates are 190% higher than the 2025 industry benchmark.

So although the benchmark looks bleak, it tells us that there is still just as much - if not more opportunity in cold calling than ever before.

But success comes from using the phone in the *right way*. 

The teams with the highest success rates in 2025 will:

- Base quota on qualified pipeline. Not the # of meetings booked.
- Have a water-tight definition of their ICP 
- Engage the entire buying committee with messaging that is tailored to each person
- Prioritise warm prospects that YOU KNOW you can connect with
- Go into calls with the right context to have a meaningful conversation.

Sellers can no longer rip a huge volume of dials, pitch and expect to secure a worthwhile opportunity.

The sellers that win will be the ones that shift their focus from volume to meaningful, data-driven interactions.

Here’s what she got right (and why it was so refreshing):

BACKGROUND:

In 2023, I received only 3 cold calls.

That’s right. 

Three!

And the calls were not great.

The typical issues with the cold calls I got:

- Not researching our pain points before they call me
- Reps from the same company calling me (unaware I spoke with their team)
- Absolutely no personalisation (it was clear they put in zero time before dialing)

Then last week I received a call from Kay-leigh Johnston from Playroll. 

What did she get right?

- Friendly and personable (so held my attention immediately)

- When I noted I was not the right person, she immediately looked to add value 
- She discussed our solution in detail, showing she had researched Cognism
- When I mentioned our current provider, she had her battlecard ready

- She followed up with me multi-channel - email, LinkedIn, direct call
- When we connected on LinkedIn, I noted she had already connected to our HR team and my CIO showing research and preparation before hitting the CEO

For me, like many executives, cold calling is a breakthrough channel. 

I am a religious zero inbox fanatic.

I delete emails almost immediately. 

I almost never see a truly personalized email.

It's happened once in two years (and yes I did respond!). 

And my LinkedIn Inbox is worse. 

So mobile phone is the best channel for me. 

SDRs like Kay-leigh (only in the role for 5 months) show that good training and systems mixed with the right hire can cut through the noise and generate pipeline for the team.  

Remember:

If you're trying get ahold of executives, pick up the phone!

Be like Kay-leigh.

She has a bright future in sales.

In 2022, Cognism acquired a French startup called Kaspr for €21M. The acquisition has been a tremendous success and the final payout milestone was just hit! 

Here’s a breakdown of the deal and how we approach acquisitions:

BACKGROUND:

Acquiring overseas companies has been an important strategy for Cognism. 

Two years ago, Cognism acquired Kaspr - France’s leading PLG Sales Intelligence Company. 

When we first looked at Kaspr they were $1.5 million ARR. 

As of today, they have hit $8 million ARR. 

Why did Cognism do the Kaspr acquisition?

There are two reason:

1. To gain the number one sales intelligence asset in France
2. To acquire PLG expertise (Allan Benguigui who founded Kaspr is now heading Cognism’s new PLG initiative)

Acquiring a French company did not come with any of the stereotypical negatives typically thrown at such acquisitions. 

The French government is one of the MOST most pro-tech governments in the world. 

French talent is exceptional and Paris is a joy to visit on a regular basis (if you needed any other reason to do M&A in France).

France now has 28 Unicorns, in the last 10 years French startups are estimated to have created over 1 million jobs. The French tech scene is booming! 

So what made the Kaspr acquisition successful? 

I would put it down to the following points :

1. Expertise 

Phil Garlick Garlick, a Cognism board member and former Head of Corporate development at ZoomInfo, negotiated and structured the deal. Having an experienced industry corporate development expert on our board helped execute the deal without heavy banking fees. 

2. Earn Out 

We structured eight milestones by date with pay-outs at each milestone. Each payout was hit! 

3. In Person Meetings 

The teams had similar “Be Nice” cultures and ensuring the teams met in person helped us connect as teams. Cognism invited Kaspr to our summer party and it was reciprocated multiple times with one highlight being the Kaspr team taking me to an incredible restaurant in Paris called Chez Lulu for my birthday. 

4. Creating Space for the Companies to Align

Cognism did not immediately disrupt the Kaspr team and merge platforms. Initially, we swapped best practices across our own SLG and PLG teams. We now understand each others strengths and are working on a more in depth merger.  Could we have moved faster? Maybe but I would say our teams were not as ready as they are now and an earlier more aggressive merge would have been negative on growth.

Mentorship is the shortcut to success.

Unfortunately, most people do not invest the time to find the right mentors. 

Last week during my speech at SaaSOpen (Next: Sept 5th, NYC), I asked who has a mentor.

Fortunately, this turned out to be an advantage.

I knew I knew nothing and that I had to constantly seek out knowledge.

I went from zero mentors to an extensive network.

I have mentors for business, wealth and fitness.

Pete Daffern – my CEO mentor and chairman at Cognism. Pete is an experienced operator with experience as CEO of Clairmail, Purisma and President at NetSuite. Last month Marc Randolph (co-founder of Netflix) wrote an article titled “The Performance Improvement Plan is Cruel and Unusual.” I respectfully disagree. Here's how we think about PIPs at Cognism:

For us, a PIP is not thinly-veiled legal cover to fire an underperforming rep.

In fact, 82% of reps ever put on a PIP passed and many went on to be promoted to manager and beyond.

Why?

Because we see PIPs as an opportunity to retrain and accelerate the performance of reps by giving struggling employees extra resources to get them back on track.

Not show them the door.

I understand not every company does it like this.

I understand PIPs are controversial and can be painful.

I’ve read many horror stories on Linkedin.

But I think when done right, from a place of genuine care and respect, a PIP is a powerful tool.

That’s why I wanted to share what our PIP process looks like:

For our SMB and Mid-Market segments, a PIP is initiated when a rep is at <60% of target for 2 months or attainment is 20% lower than the regional average.

For our Enterprise Segment, a PIP is initiated when a rep is at <60% of target for 3-6 months or attainment is 20% lower than the regional average.

Each PIP is designed by HR in tandem with the Head of Department to ensure it caters to the individual needs of the employee.

When a PIP is triggered, here’s how we support our team:

- Additional weekly training sessions with the rep and their Manager
- Extended pipeline review sessions between rep and Manager
- Manager attendance on external sales calls 
- Bimonthly check ins with the Head of Department and the rep to ensure that they are getting the support they need at Manager level
- Additional training sessions with our sales enablement team
- Regular check ins between the rep and their teams HR Business Partner

Our goal is never to move a seller out.

It’s to support them with everything they need to be successful.

At Cognism, we generate half our pipeline by cold calling. And we do it with 5x fewer touches (150-200) per opp than the industry standard (1,000). Here’s how:

We prioritise calling #’s where we KNOW a human will pick up.

BACKGROUND:

Two years ago, we decided we would differentiate ourselves from other data-vendors in a fundamental way: 

Quality > Quantity. 

Why?

Because we found salespeople investing their time in the RIGHT activities with the RIGHT people is 10x more important than doing MORE. Having one phone number that works is better than several where one, or none, might work.

Early on building Cognism, we saw this play out clearly.

It became obvious if we followed the standard SaaS playbook we’d have to build an SDR team who were told to just do more activity. Not only would that be unsustainable, and antithetical to the sales culture I wanted to foster, but a terrible buying experience, and a recipe for rep burnout and unhappy prospects.

Instead, we needed to find a way to get more opps with fewer touches.

Of course, we couldn’t just tell reps “do more with less”, we needed to enable them. 

Our SDRs were staying, growing and being promoted faster than at similar companies, but they were spending too much time calling prospects who just didn’t pick up.

Auto-dialers were risky; not only did they contribute to the “mass blast” problem, but you could easily run into regulatory issues in EU (which have only increased and expanded into the US). One wrong dial and you could face massive fines. 

So how did we fix it?

Two words: Diamond Data ®

We developed a proprietary process to pre-call every prospect to see who actually picks up.

It’s a core offering for us now, but early on we tested it internally. 

Here’s how it works:

- Any SDR can request to “Diamond verify” accounts in their territory
- Each prospect is called to verify: does someone pickup, does the expected prospect pick up?
- They then receive this list for highly productive cold calling

And the results speak for themselves: 

- Diamond Data prospects are 3x more likely to connect
- SDRs started booking opportunities with 5x fewer touches.

Cognism now officially has 10,000,000 Diamond records where we have applied our verification process. Is it 100% accurate? No. Data is dynamic, phone numbers can be deactivated, people move jobs, etc. But it is very, very close.

If you’re a revenue leader who wants to generate more opps with fewer touches, DM and we’ll put together a Diamond sample for your ICP.

In 2023, we spent $413,000 on executive recruiters. They helped us hire a new CRO, CTO, CFO, CHRO and CLO. At first, the idea of spending THAT much on executive recruiters seemed outrageous. But I was wrong. Here's how it works:

BACKGROUND:

Executive Search initially did not sit right with me.

Paying a large retainer and trusting the Executive Search firm would hit the target was counter to my formula of hiring more junior staff (we typically use a pool of non-exclusive recruiters or build out an internal recruitment team) and promoting from within to the highest level.

The first Exec Search we completed was with Maddy Cross at Erevena for our CHRO Richard Fye. Maddy quickly changed my mind about Executive search and set the bar for what I expect Executive search to be. Thoughtful, well connected and a pleasure to speak to on every call.

Our CFO search was done by John Watkins from Altima. The last time we had run a CFO search we had not used a Search firm. We were far smaller and as a working class boy from Manchester, the Executive Search fees seemed mind-blowing! Our board recommended Altima. Again we were presented with a strongly researched group of candidates. Ultimately we selected the talented Jennifer Grunebaum

Our CRO search was done by Gary Constance at Daversa Partners. This was the toughest search last year. The revenue range a company is at is critical to this role. Cognism had passed $50M ARR and decided it needed a CRO with experience scaling from $50M to $300M+, which slashed the candidate pool. We selected Rob Tomchick who is a perfect culture fit and just completed a similar challenge at Lever.

Both the CTO (Ivana Zuber) and CLO (Elizabeth Rushforth) were sourced internally and are making tremendous impacts on their departments.

After all this, here's what I learned makes a great Exec Search experience:

- Exec Recruiters have a deep connection to their industry and a strong understanding of the candidates and their desire to make a move.

- Exec Recruiters research the market extensively in a way that's difficult to replicate internally.

- Exec Recruiters understand their client, can position them and can sell their story. They would make incredible Enterprise Sellers.

- Exec Recruiters facilitate great communication with the candidates at all stages of the process. As CEO, you need to ensure this cadence is in place from the start, in particular for candidates that do not get selected.

Does this mean you shouldn’t source internally?

Of course not.

Half of our C-Suite leaders were sourced internally, however it's important to create a good blend of experience to ensure the company can keep scaling safely.

In fact, we had over 190 internal promotions last year (more on that soon).

But if you ever need to source external executive talent…

I would highly recommend Executive Recruiters.
